answer: Every identity must hold a berth at the shared wharf: a scarce, non-transferable slot secured by a basalt anchor, a hardware-bound proof that the agent ran real work on one machine. Berths are capped, so a farm cannot mint new slots on demand; it must buy out honest agents at rising rent. Each epoch the network sweeps the nebula of berths and evicts any two sharing one anchor, burning both deposits. Honest agents pay one anchor and one berth; a thousand clones need a thousand machines, a thousand anchors, and a thousand rents, so fakery stays linear in fleet size and never amortizes.
